palace-parliament.name: Palace of the Parliament & Piața Constituției
palace-parliament.blurb: The heaviest building on Earth seen from the vast square at the head of Bulevardul Unirii.

footprint.note: ~440 m E-W x 410 m N-S. West edge cuts through the palace east wing so the whole 270 m main façade (east) stands inside the scene; the square, the head of Bulevardul Unirii with its first fountains, and the two curved 9-storey Ceaușescu-era blocks on Bd. Libertății frame it. Player is fenced out of the palace grounds except the public sidewalk; the visitor entrance (tours) is on the north side, Str. Izvor 2-4 / Bd. Națiunile Unite.

structures.name: Palatul Parlamentului (east/main façade)

dims.height_note: 84 m (en wiki) / 86 m above ground (ro wiki); 9 levels above ground + 9 underground (ro wiki), 92 m deep; OSM height=29 is the eave of the outer wings only

structures.style: Monumental socialist-realist neoclassicism (1984-1997), chief architect Anca Petrescu
structures.massing: Stepped ziggurat-like mass: wide 4-5 storey outer ring of wings, then set-back tiers climbing to a central cubic block crowned by a square attic/tower on the main E-W axis. East façade symmetric about the axis of Bulevardul Unirii; central projecting entrance pavilion (official entrance C4) with a tall colonnaded loggia/balcony (Sala A. I. Cuza opens onto it) above a ceremonial ramp and stair.

facade.material: light stone cladding over concrete (marble/travertine-like dressing, Romanian stone)
facade.windows: Very long regular rows of tall round-headed (arched) windows between paired pilasters/half-columns on every tier; dark bronze-tinted glazing (#3B3A36) in bronze/brown frames; ground storey rusticated with arcades
facade.ornament: Repeating colonnades and balustrades on each set-back terrace (white balusters), cornices with dentils, carved stone garlands, Romanian (Brâncovenesc) floral motifs in panels, three tall flagpoles on the forecourt facing the square (Romanian tricolour between two blue flags - EU and NATO, photo Bucharest Constitution Square.jpg); front garden: large flower parterre in red/gold, clipped hedges and conical thujas, a promenade and ground floodlights
facade.roof: Flat terraces behind balustrades; central tower block flat roof (panoramic terrace tour)

signage: PARLAMENTUL ROMÂNIEI (small brass/stone lettering at the official entrances)
Camera Deputaților / Senatul României plates at gates
CIC - Centrul de Informare a Cetățenilor (visitor centre, north side)

structures.name: Piața Constituției

dims.note: OSM polygon (N-S long axis); used as paid surface parking (OSM amenity=parking, fee=yes) most of the year, cleared for events

structures.surface: granite setts (OSM surface=sett), grey; painted white parking bay lines when used as a car park
structures.events: Christmas Market (Târgul de Crăciun București) 29 Nov-28 Dec in 2025 with >120 wooden cabins, a 30 m tree, carousel; National Day military parade (1 Dec) and big open-air concerts are staged here

structures.name: Ceasul "București 1459"
structures.note: 4-faced analog pole clock at the east edge of the square; "1459" = first documentary mention of Bucharest (Vlad III charter of 20 Sep 1459)

structures.name: Bulevardul Unirii fountains (head of the axis)
structures.note: Two rows of jet nozzles in the boulevard median start ~170 m east of the square centre; the full 3.5 km boulevard fountain chain with the Piața Unirii "Fountain Show" (Simfonia Apei) is one of the most-searched attractions (Visit Bucharest 2022/2024) - show is in the Unirii district, here only the first basins (light grey granite basins, jets 1-4 m).

structures.name: Curved 9-storey government blocks on Bd. Libertății

facade.material: stuccoed concrete with stone-clad ground floor, regular vertical window bands, brown/bronze frames

structures.note: Backdrop wrapping the square north and south (ministries: Finance, Justice, Regional Development etc.)

ground.surface: granite setts ~10x10 cm laid in rows/fan arcs

ground.markings: white lane lines, zebra crossings (white bars), 3+3 lanes

ground.surface: sloped lawns, gravel/asphalt service roads, retaining walls and terraces (OSM retaining_wall, hedges)

vegetation.summary: Palace slope gardens: 355 OSM-mapped trees in the footprint, mostly Quercus robur (62), Tilia tomentosa (48), Thuja orientalis (43, clipped conical rows), Tilia platyphyllos (37), Sambucus nigra, Populus tremula/alba, Acer negundo; clipped box/privet hedges (30 OSM hedge ways). Square itself is treeless (open setts).

street_furniture: tall boulevard lamp posts (double-arm, ~10-12 m, dark grey) along Bd. Libertății/Unirii
white backless benches (OSM colour=white) on the park side
lift gates/barriers at palace service entrances, guard booths, steel fence (dark green/black palisade) around the palace grounds
drinking fountain (bubbler) at the square east edge
flagpoles; in December: wooden market cabins, 30 m tree, carousel
palace-parliament.lighting: Night: palace façade floodlit warm white/amber from ground projectors; boulevard sodium/LED lamps; square lit by mast lights; December adds string lights over the market.
palace-parliament.backdrop: North/south: curved 9-storey ministry blocks (cream). East: Bulevardul Unirii axis lined with 8-10 storey 1980s blocks (Bl. 1, Bl. 8A) with fountains in the median running to Piața Unirii. West: palace mass fills the view; People's Salvation Cathedral (gilded dome, 127 m) rises behind the south-west corner.

crowd.typical: Sparse on weekdays (the square is huge): small tour groups photographing the façade, joggers, parked-car drivers, guards. Dense on 1 December (parade) and in December evenings (Christmas market, families, Bulgarian day-trippers). ~150,000-260,000 tour visitors per year inside the palace (2023: ~152,000).

ambient_sounds: traffic hum on the Bd. Libertății ring (honks)
December: carols, mulled-wine stalls chatter, carousel organ

plaques.title: Size
plaques.text: 270 m x 240 m, 84 m tall and 92 m deep underground: one of the largest administrative buildings in the world.

plaques.title: Anca Petrescu
plaques.text: Built 1984-1997 by chief architect Anca Petrescu, who won the contest at 28, with a team of about 700 architects.

plaques.title: The heaviest building
plaques.text: It weighs about 4.1 million tonnes, the heaviest building in the world, and sinks about 6 mm every year.

plaques.title: What was lost
plaques.text: About 7 km² of old Bucharest were demolished and some 40,000 people relocated to make room for it.

plaques.title: Romanian materials
plaques.text: Made almost entirely of Romanian materials: 1,000,000 m³ of marble, 3,500 t of crystal, 480 chandeliers.

plaques.title: Not for sale
plaques.text: In 1990 Rupert Murdoch offered US$1 billion for the building. The offer was refused.

interaction.title: Pace the Palace
interaction.desc: Walk/run the full 270 m east façade between two marker plaques; a timer and pedometer compare your time with how long it takes to walk the Pentagon's side and show "this is only one side". In December the square turns into the Christmas Market: buy a cup of vin fiert (mulled wine, shown as hot cocoa for kids) and ride the carousel.
interaction.true_to_place: The size is THE experience of the place; Christmas Market is really held here (2023-2025).

photo_angle.note: From the east edge of Piața Constituției by the "București 1459" clock, ~330 m from the façade, camera on the Unirii axis so the central pavilion is centred; at dusk the floodlights turn on. Postcard alt: from the Bd. Unirii median fountains (outside footprint).

seasonal_time_of_day: Summer: harsh midday sun from the south, heat shimmer over the setts; floodlights at ~21:00.
December: Christmas Market cabins fill the square (29 Nov-28 Dec 2025 edition), 30 m tree on axis, snow possible.
1 December (National Day): military parade, tribunes, crowd barriers.
Night: façade lit, square nearly empty.
palace-parliament.copyright_note: Romania has no freedom of panorama and the architect's heirs have claimed a 2% royalty for commercial use of images of the building; non-commercial use is described as unrestricted (en wiki). Keep the game non-commercial and do not ship photos of the palace as textures.

Hi!

Oops, sorry!

Boiled corn, roasted corn!
Magnets, souvenirs, Dracula!

Hey, you knocked over my goods!
Easy, easy!
The photo is free, the magnet costs ten lei!

Last ones, I'll sell them cheaper!
Take two, I give you one free.
With poppy seeds or salt?
Hardly anyone today.
I take card too, yes.
Mulled wine, hot tea, chimney cake!
Gingerbread with the palace on it, ten lei!
lines.orig: Turtă dulce cu Palatul pe ea, zece lei!

lines.text: Merry Christmas!
The carousel is free for kids today.
lines.orig: Caruselul e gratis pentru copii azi.

lines.text: Good day!
Good day, young man.
Kiss your hand... oh, sorry, good day!
lines.orig: Sărut mâna... a, pardon, bună ziua!

lines.text: How are you? Come to see the city?
lines.orig: Ce mai faceți? Ați venit să vedeți orașul?

lines.text: Careful, dear!
Watch where you are going, young man!
Oh my, I nearly fell!
lines.orig: Vai de mine, era să cad!

lines.text: Can't you see I have my shopping bag?
lines.orig: Nu vezi că sunt cu sacoșa?

lines.text: Taking my picture? Let me fix my headscarf.
lines.orig: Mă pozezi pe mine? Stai să-mi aranjez baticul.

lines.text: Oh, I'm no film star.
Send the photo to my grandson, he has Facebook.
lines.orig: Trimite-i poza nepotului meu, are Facebook.

lines.text: In my day there were only old houses here.
lines.orig: Pe vremea mea aici erau numai case vechi.

lines.text: So hot today, what a heatwave!
lines.orig: Ce cald e azi, mamă, ce caniculă!

lines.text: The pension barely buys a loaf of bread.
lines.orig: Pensia nu ajunge nici de-o pâine.

lines.text: The doctor told me to walk every day.
lines.orig: Mi-a zis doctorul să merg pe jos zilnic.

lines.text: Tomorrow I'm going to the market, maybe I'll find good tomatoes.
lines.orig: Mâine merg la piață, poate găsesc roșii bune.

lines.text: These young people only look at their phones.
lines.orig: Tinerii ăștia numai în telefon se uită.

lines.text: My granddaughter is calling, let's see how she is.
lines.orig: Sună nepoata, să vedem ce mai face.

lines.text: God help us keep our health.
I worked here as a young man, on the building site, three shifts.
lines.orig: Eu am lucrat aici ca tânăr, pe șantier, în trei schimburi.

lines.text: We called it the People's House, now the Palace of the Parliament.
lines.orig: Casa Poporului îi ziceam, acum Palatul Parlamentului.

lines.text: Mihai Vodă monastery stood here; they moved it on rails.
lines.orig: Aici a fost Mănăstirea Mihai Vodă, au mutat-o pe șine.

lines.text: How big it is! — And that's only one side.

lines.text: Shall we go to the Cathedral too? — It's right behind.
lines.orig: Mergem și la Catedrală? — E chiar în spate.

peoples-salvation-cathedral.name: People's Salvation Cathedral (National Cathedral)
peoples-salvation-cathedral.blurb: The tallest and largest Orthodox church in the world (127 m), with a gilded dome rising behind the Palace of the Parliament.

footprint.note: ~400 m x 420 m on Dealul Arsenalului: the cathedral (121 x 71 m footprint), its 11,600 m² piazza, the underground-chapel entrances and Calea 13 Septembrie with its 9-11 storey 1980s blocks to the south as backdrop; the Palace of the Parliament south façade bounds the north-east view.

structures.name: Catedrala Națională
structures.style: Romanian revival synthesis: Renaissance-revival high dome on a drum with a 16-arch peristyle, Romanesque façade towers, Neo-Byzantine bell tower; six octagonal towers around the dome; bell tower (campanile) at the west end

facade.material: light stone cladding (cream/white) over brick masonry
facade.dome: cupolas clad in Tecu Gold brass (gilded copper look), ribbed with embossed medallion panels and a decorated gold band at the base; tower drums white with arched windows between engaged colonnettes (photo June 2023)
facade.cross: 7 m / 7 t gilded cross installed 8 April 2025
facade.doors: 27 double-leaf 5.5 m-high bronze-plated doors with 61 saint bas-reliefs
facade.window: Ascension stained-glass window 5.5 x 15 m above the main entrance
facade.mosaics_exterior: mosaic icons in lunettes over portals

structures.bells: 6 bells totalling 32.2 t; the largest 25.19 t at 60 m in the bell tower, heard 15-20 km away

structures.name: Piazza (esplanade)
structures.osm: relation/16698908 (highway=pedestrian area 13,270 m² around the church)

structures.name: Paraclisul Catedralei (temporary wooden chapel/annex)
structures.note: smaller church/chapel at the site edge on Calea 13 Septembrie, height 4 m per OSM

vegetation.summary: 174 OSM trees: rows of Tilia cordata (81) and Aesculus hippocastanum (78) along Calea 13 Septembrie and the slopes; Fraxinus americana, Quercus robur, Rhus typhina.

street_furniture: candle-lighting stands (lumânărar) in a separate pavilion
bus stop "Palatul Parlamentului" (route 136) on Calea 13 Septembrie
peoples-salvation-cathedral.lighting: Dome and towers floodlit golden at night, visible across the city.
peoples-salvation-cathedral.backdrop: North: Palace of the Parliament south façade (Calea 13 Septembrie entrance); south: 9-11 storey 1980s apartment blocks (Bl. 53-91) with ground-floor shops (Mega Image, Help Net pharmacy).

crowd.typical: Pilgrims and worshippers, especially on Sundays, feast days (Ascension = Heroes' Day, St Andrew 30 Nov) and since the 2025 consecration; tourists coming from the Palace; priests and nuns; candle and icon stalls.

ambient_sounds: bells (deep 25 t bell) at service times
Byzantine chant from loudspeakers on feast days

plaques.title: 127 metres
plaques.text: At 127 m (133 m to the top of the cross) it is the tallest and largest Orthodox church building in the world.

plaques.title: Murano mosaics
plaques.text: It holds the world's largest collection of church mosaics, about 25,000 m², made with Venetian Murano glass.

plaques.title: The great bell
plaques.text: The main bell weighs 25.19 t, was cast in Innsbruck in 2016 and can be heard 15-20 km away.

plaques.title: Consecrated
plaques.text: The altar was consecrated on 25 November 2018; the mosaics on 26 October 2025, when the cathedral opened permanently.

plaques.title: The piazza
plaques.text: The 11,600 m² piazza can hold over 23,000 people; the whole 11-hectare complex 125,000.

interaction.title: Light a candle & ring time
interaction.desc: Light a candle at the candle pavilion (for the living on one side, the departed on the other - a real Orthodox custom), then stand on the piazza at noon to hear the great bell. Quiet zone: no running on the piazza steps during services.
interaction.true_to_place: Candle-lighting and the record bell are what visitors do and talk about.

photo_angle.note: From the south-west corner of the piazza (OSM pedestrian area relation/16698908, 13,270 m² wrapping the church) looking ENE at the west front: bell tower (86 m) over the main portal with the Ascension stained-glass window, gilded central dome behind. Calea 13 Septembrie runs ~130 m south; Parcul Catedralei (under construction) lies north towards the Palace.

seasonal_time_of_day: 30 November (St Andrew) and Ascension: huge pilgrim crowds.
Easter night: candle-lit Resurrection service on the piazza.
Summer: heat on the open stone piazza.
peoples-salvation-cathedral.copyright_note: Recent copyrighted architecture (no freedom of panorama in Romania): reference only.

culture.note: "Bună ziua" (good day) is the safe greeting with strangers; "Salut"/"Hey" among young people. Use "dumneavoastră" (formal you) with older people; elderly men may still say "Sărut mâna" (I kiss your hand) to women as an old-fashioned courtesy. Thank you = "Mulțumesc" or the very common French loan "Mersi".
Bună dimineața (morning), Bună ziua (day), Bună seara (evening); Noapte bună only when parting at night. Pick by the scene clock.

Romanian is a Romance language; young educated people usually speak good English, older educated people often French/Italian/Spanish. Italians/Spanish tourists often half-understand Romanian signs. So bubbles: Romanian for locals with English translation; tourists speak their own language.

Foreign visitors to Bucharest searching online in 2024 came mostly from UK, US, Germany, Bulgaria, Italy, Greece, Israel, Netherlands and France; British searched for Therme, Americans for "Wednesday" filming locations and Romanian food, Bulgarians for Christmas markets/concerts. Use these origins for tourist personas.
Never assume a car will stop at a crosswalk; drivers can be inconsiderate. Locals joke and grumble about traffic, honking, sidewalk parking and buses; keep it good-humoured, never aggressive.

Typical words: mici/mititei (grilled minced-meat rolls), ciorbă de burtă (tripe soup), sarmale (cabbage rolls), papanași (doughnuts with sour cream and jam), covrigi (pretzels sold from street windows). Caru' cu Bere, Berăria H and Hanu' lui Manuc were the most-searched restaurants by foreign tourists in 2024.

Orthodox churches (Stavropoleos, Patriarchal/National Cathedral): people cross themselves when passing, speak quietly, women often cover their heads, shoulders/knees covered; avoid flash and ask before photographing services. Nuns/priests are greeted with "Bună ziua" or "Doamne-ajută" (God help); do not script jokes about clergy.
culture.source: general Orthodox etiquette (no single source fetched from this environment - verify with church staff signage)

culture.note: Romanians are hospitable and insist when offering something ("no" is often treated as politeness and the offer repeated) - vendors/elders can repeat an offer once before accepting a refusal. Respect for the elderly is valued; older men may kiss a lady's hand; handshakes are standard.

Vlad the Impaler is seen by many Romanians as a national hero; some are offended when he is equated with Count Dracula - so locals in bubbles push back ("Vlad Țepeș was one of ours, not a vampire!"). Opinions on Ceaușescu vary; some older people speak of him positively - an elder persona may be nostalgic, others critical; never caricature either.
Avoid lines implying Romanian is Slavic or that Romania was part of the USSR; never confuse Romanians with Roma people.
Unsolicited offers of help/taxis near tourist areas can be scams; locals recommend Bolt/Uber. A vendor/tout persona may push magnets or taxis politely; the player can just walk away.

Communism and Ceaușescu are top tourist interests ("Communism and communist buildings remain at the top of searches"). Locals talk about it with dark irony (e.g. calling the Memorial of Rebirth "the impaled potato"), but lines must stay factual and avoid mocking victims of 1989 (around 1,500 died).

Do not use ethnic jokes (in particular about Roma people) or Dracula/vampire clichés aimed at locals; Dracula appears only as souvenir-vendor patter and as a historical fact (Vlad III built the Old Princely Court).

1 March: mărțișor (red-and-white string trinkets) sold everywhere and given to women; December: "Crăciun fericit!" and the Christmas market in Piața Constituției; winter: "Ce ger!" (what frost); summer heatwaves: "caniculă" (summers often exceed 30 °C).
